findings.claim: The declared objective is final predicted target affinity as primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; the reward view is the endpoint pointcloud with a detached FLOWR endpoint VJP, so coordinate contrasts below are selection/geometry descriptors, not affinity benefits.

Continuous landmark coordinate features over the observed window are non-monotone: landmark_00_soft_mass shows 4 sign changes with a positive early rate (first_rate_z ~ +9.3) reversing to a negative late rate (last_rate_z ~ -10.0), and landmark_00_local_dy shows 6 sign changes with a strongly negative early rate (first_rate_z ~ -72.4) reversing to positive late (last_rate_z ~ +5.5). A constant rule is therefore not supported; a time-conditioned rule is favored, but no polynomial was accepted and extrapolation is disallowed.

Branch-adjusted raw-covariance contrasts at the global centroid are null: global_centroid_x/y/z have CIs spanning zero (p ~ 0.55-0.95, q ~ 0.69-0.97) with same-sign batch fractions near 0.36-0.50, so no signed favorable-versus-comparison centroid contrast is established.

Shape covariance contrasts are the only branch-adjusted features with consistent sign: shape_yy is negative with CI entirely below zero (p ~ 0.048, q ~ 0.153) and same-sign batch fraction ~0.79, and shape_xx is negative with CI below zero (p ~ 0.096, q ~ 0.232, same-sign ~0.79). These are marginal geometric descriptors that survive multiplicity adjustment only weakly (q > 0.05).

Ranking by point estimate alone would elevate the large-magnitude centroid and local-derivative features, but multiplicity-adjusted support (q values) and same-sign batch fractions reorder the priority toward the shape_xx/shape_yy contrasts; the centroid features are not credible despite their larger raw means.

hypotheses.direction: time-conditioned sign reversal of the landmark contrast
hypotheses.falsifier: No sign reversal in the observed-node contrast values, or a constant rule fitting the observed nodes within the reported node RMSE.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_soft_mass and landmark_00_local_dy contrast values at observed score nodes
hypotheses.scope: observed window [0.0,0.5], predicted endpoint world coordinates
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned coordinate contrast on landmark_00_soft_mass and landmark_00_local_dy (early-window versus late-window sign) better describes the observed selection-node geometry than a constant contrast rule.

hypotheses.falsifier: CI spanning zero or same-sign batch fraction near 0.5 for shape_xx/shape_yy under the same adjustment.
hypotheses.observable: branch-adjusted raw covariance of shape_xx and shape_yy
hypotheses.statement: A signed shape-covariance contrast (shape_yy, shape_xx negative) is a more reproducible coordinate descriptor than global-centroid contrasts.

limitations: No decoded terminal labels or final affinity outcomes are supplied; last-record and survival credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit, and the immediate-versus-descendant comparison is unavailable.
Continuous-trend rows read are limited to landmark_00 features; other landmark and regional features were not inspected, so the non-monotonicity finding is not generalized beyond the read features.
All contrasts are coordinate/selection descriptors under the endpoint-VJP reward; they are not physical interaction energies or evidence of neural-module causation.
No temperature or executable-source change is proposed; temperatures are immutable task parameters.
